create_media_systems.ponder.jukebox.head: Streaming Custom Discs
create_media_systems.ponder.jukebox.text: Use a Custom Disc in the air to write a YouTube or Discord link onto it. The server checks that the link plays before writing it.
In any jukebox it streams to everyone nearby: loud up close, fading out with distance.
To limit who hears it, right-click the jukebox with a Jukebox Range Quill to pick it.
Then select two corners like with the Schematic and Quill, and right-click again to set the volume. Only players inside the range hear it.
Right-click the picked jukebox again without a selection to change just the volume, or reset the range.
create_media_systems.ponder.speakers.tex: A Disc Reader plays a Custom Disc without making a sound itself...
...for the Speakers linked to it. Speakers also work with a jukebox, playing in sync with it.
With the Range Quill, pick the source, then right-click each speaker to link it and set its volume and channel.
Set one to Left and one to Right for stereo, or leave them on Mix.
Turn a speaker with a Wrench. It is loudest in front and quiet behind.
create_media_systems.ponder.line_mixer.h: Mixing Sources with the Line Mixer
create_media_systems.ponder.line_mixer.t: A Line Mixer, two blocks wide, mixes several sources into one line for the speakers linked to it.
With the Range Quill, pick a source, then right-click a channel of the mixer to plug it in. Its lamp lights. Doing the same again unplugs it.
Right-click its master section to pick the mixer itself, then each speaker to link it. The speakers play everything plugged in.
Point at a fader, hold right-click and look along it: the knob follows, and everyone hears it at once. A channel's fader sets how loud its source is, the master's how loud they all are.
The meter beside each fader shows what its channel passes on, and the master's what the mixer does, to whoever hears it.
Another Line Mixer set against its left side is an extension: seven more channels under the same master. More can follow it.
create_media_systems.ponder.train_disc_r: An Announcement Schedule is edited like a Train Schedule: add a station, then announcements for the trip there, each with its own link: on departure, after N seconds, at N%% of the way, N seconds before arrival, or on arrival.
Put it in a Train Disc Reader on the carriage. It can be swapped even after the train is assembled.
Train Speakers on the same train play it, without linking. Each is heard only in its own carriage.
To set their volume, hold right-click on the reader with a Wrench while the train is disassembled.
When the train departs for or arrives at a matching station, the announcement plays, fading in and out as riders get on and off. Several readers play at once.
Play at N% of the way

create_media_systems.ponder.train_detect: Place a Train Detector like a Train Observer: right-click the track first, then place it nearby.
Give the detector and a Train Signal Receiver the same channel (empty hand). Receivers can be anywhere.
While a train is over the detector, every receiver on its channel gives a redstone signal of 15. Distance and unloaded chunks don't matter.

create_media_systems.ponder.equalizer.te: An Equalizer touching a Blu-ray Player turns the Low, Mid and Hi of its sound up or down, on its displays and speakers alike.
Point at a fader, hold right-click and look along it: the knob follows, showing you its gain, and everyone hears it once you let go. Each goes up or down by up to 12 dB.
A second Equalizer touching the first splits each band in two and takes the lower half: BASS, Low-Mid and Hi-Mid. More than two do nothing.
Sneak to place a block on its top instead. Through Engineer's Goggles it shows each band's gain.
create_media_systems.ponder.blu_ray_play: DVDs, Blu-rays and the Blu-ray Player
Use a DVD or a Blu-ray in the air to write its playlist, one video link per row, or a YouTube playlist link to fill it with the playlist's videos. The server checks every link before writing them.
A DVD holds 16 videos played at up to 480p, and a Blu-ray 64 at up to 1080p. Neither plays in a jukebox.
Right-click a Blu-ray Player with either disc to play its videos one after another; it stops after the last. Right-click with an empty hand to take the disc out.

Its volume is set like any Create value: hold right-click on its top with a Wrench. It turns its displays and its speakers up or down alike. Its front sets how brightly its displays light their surroundings, the same for everyone; 0%% turns it off.
Shift+right-click it with a Remote to pair them. Use the Remote in the air for its buttons: previous, play/pause, stop, next, play a video by number, and volume.
A Remote reaches its Blu-ray Player only within the server's range (64 blocks unless set otherwise).
Through Engineer's Goggles it shows which video it plays, and how loud.
create_media_systems.ponder.display.head: Displays
create_media_systems.ponder.display.text: A Display goes on the side of a wall, where it shows a Blu-ray Player's video.
Hold a Display Quill, right-click a Blu-ray Player to pick it, then right-click displays to link them; again to unlink. Any number of displays can show one player.
Looking at a display with the quill, Ctrl+scroll makes it a block wider or narrower (a sixteenth with Shift). It grows right and up, and its height follows its ratio.
Shift+right-click steps through the ratios: free, 16:9, 4:3, 21:9, 1:1, and the video's own. Alt+scroll sets the height alone.
Its sound comes from the middle of the picture, at the player's volume. While a speaker plays that Blu-ray Player, only the speakers are heard.

create_media_systems.ponder.image_viewer: An Image Viewer goes on the side of a wall like a Display, and shows a picture from a link.
Right-click it with a Wrench to type the image's link: a PNG, JPEG, GIF (its first frame) or BMP, from a site the server allows. Each player's game downloads it.
Size it with a Display Quill, just like a display. Shift+right-click's last ratio is the image's own.
Right-click it with the quill to take its frame away: only the picture is left, and the wall shows through where the image is transparent. Right-click again to put the frame back.
Through Engineer's Goggles it shows its link and size.
create_media_systems.ponder.lighting_con: A Lighting Console is 4 desks wide and 2 deep, all facing the same way, with a Lighting Console Monitor on each desk of the back row. It comes together as soon as the last block is in place.
Point at its controls with an empty hand or a Wrench: right-click buttons and pads, scroll over a value to change it, and hold right-click to move a fader or the aim pad.
Its faders set each of the six groups' brightness and the master. The rest, on the desk and the monitors, set the selected group's colours, presets, motion, aim, and how it follows sound and video.
Through Engineer's Goggles it shows the selected group and how many fixtures are linked.
create_media_systems.ponder.stage_lights: Stage Lights and the Tuning Wrench
Moving Head Lights, Strip Lights and Laser Projectors light up the stage. A Lighting Console drives up to 64 of them, in six groups.
Hold a Tuning Wrench and right-click a finished console to pick it.
Then right-click fixtures to link them to the group selected on the console. Right-click one again, or Shift+right-click it, to unlink it.

Right-click a Blu-ray Player, a Disc Reader or a jukebox to link it too. Turn on sound or video linking on the console, and the lights follow its music or its picture's colours. Shift+right-click a Blu-ray Player to link only its picture.
Looking at a fixture with an empty hand, scroll to move it to another group. Shift+scroll changes its place in the group's order, and Ctrl+scroll the colour it takes from the group.
Right-click a player with the Tuning Wrench to have the selected group follow them, or Shift+right-click the air to be followed yourself.
Place a fixture under a ceiling to hang it upside down. Through Engineer's Goggles it shows its group and order.

create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_1: A hi-fi stack is separate units in one block: place one, then use the next on it. A whole set of five fills the block. Any order works, and any unit can be left out.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_2: Sneak and right-click it with an empty hand to take the top unit off again.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_3: Every unit but the amplifier needs its flat cable: use an Audio Cable on the socket at its back. The disc player needs its line cable too, or it plays unheard. Right-click a plug to pull it out.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_4: For sound, use an Audio Cable on one of the amplifier's speaker terminals, then on a hi-fi speaker: one for the left, one for the right. Sneak and right-click a speaker with an empty hand to pull its cable out.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_5: Point at a button and right-click to press it. Hold right-click on a knob and look left or right to turn it. What you point at is named above the hotbar.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_6: Open the disc player's tray and put a CD, DVD, Blu-ray or Custom Disc on it. A DVD or Blu-ray also shows on displays linked to the stack with a Display Quill.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_7: Put a Cassette Tape in either deck. A tape remembers where it was stopped, so rewind it to hear it from the top.
create_media_systems.ponder.hifi.text_8: The amplifier picks what is heard and how loud. The sound controller shapes it with its presets and shows its spectrum. A Remote paired with the stack works its disc player and volume from afar.

create_media_systems.keyboard.control.ba: BANK ◄: the previous of the 16 pad banks.
BANK ►: the next of the 16 pad banks.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.sn: SNAP SHOT: recall one of 8 stored panel settings. Press it, a pad, then NEXT. With SHIFT lit, stores the current settings on that pad instead.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.pr: PREV (EXIT): leaves snapshot mode without doing anything.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.ne: NEXT (ENTER): recalls or stores the snapshot on the pad picked.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.pr: PROG CHG: the pads pick the sound of the framed zone. 16 banks of 8 cover all 128 General MIDI sounds.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.cc: CC: the pads switch controllers on and off for the framed zone. Bank 1: damper, sostenuto, soft, modulation, reverb, chorus.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.sh: SHIFT: click to light it, then: UPPER 1 turns the arpeggiator on or off, OCT -/+ picks the velocity curve, SPLIT lets the next key set the split point, SNAP SHOT stores.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.fu: FUNC: click to light it, then press the key under one of the functions it shows above the keys.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.kn: R1 CUTOFF: how bright the framed zone sounds. Drag up and down, or scroll.
R2 RESONANCE of the framed zone's filter.
R3 ATTACK: how slowly the framed zone's notes come in.
R4 RELEASE: how long the framed zone's notes ring after a key is let go.
R5 REVERB of the framed zone.
R6 CHORUS of the framed zone.
R7 PAN: the framed zone to the left or right speaker.
R8 VOLUME of the framed zone.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.lo: LOWER zone and its sound: click to turn it on and frame it for the pads and knobs; click the framed zone again to turn it off. Zones that are on play layered.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.up: UPPER 1 zone and its sound: click to turn it on and frame it for the pads and knobs; click the framed zone again to turn it off. With SHIFT lit: the arpeggiator.
UPPER 2 zone and its sound: click to turn it on and frame it for the pads and knobs; click the framed zone again to turn it off.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.sp: SPLIT: LOWER plays the keys up to the split point, the UPPER zones those above. With SHIFT lit, the next key pressed becomes the split point.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.tr: TRANSPOSE: click to light it, then OCT -/+ shift the keys by semitones (-6 to +5).
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.s1: S1: sends controller 80 while held. With the arpeggiator on: HOLD.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.s2: S2: sends controller 81 while held. With the arpeggiator on: TAP TEMPO.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.oc: OCTAVE -: an octave down (to -4). With TRANSPOSE lit a semitone down, with SHIFT lit a lighter velocity curve.
OCTAVE +: an octave up (to +5). With TRANSPOSE lit a semitone up, with SHIFT lit a heavier velocity curve.
create_media_systems.keyboard.control.le: Pitch bend / modulation lever: drag left and right to bend, push it away to add vibrato.
create_media_systems.ponder.midi_keyboar: The keyboard is three blocks wide in one block: set it on a desk with room to either side. Right-click it to play, or join someone already playing.

Its keys, pads, knobs and buttons are worked with the mouse. The computer's keyboard plays it too: the rows from Z and from Q are its keys, Space its damper pedal. A real MIDI keyboard plugged into the computer plays it as well.
It sounds from itself. To play it through speakers, pick it with a Range Quill, then right-click each speaker: set one to the left channel and one to the right.
Everyone nearby hears and sees what is played, as it is played. The pads pick the sound: 128 of them, in 16 banks of 8.
Here is a piano piece played on it.
create_media_systems.ponder.px_s1100.tex: It needs power: feed Forge Energy into the back of its bass side, or right-click it with a charged Battery.
Or set an AC Adapter on the floor right behind it. The adapter runs on a shaft turning below it, on Forge Energy, or on furnace fuel right-clicked into it.
A real MIDI keyboard plugged into the computer plays it too: pick the device in the Settings of its screen.
Turn it on with its power button, then right-click it to play with the mouse or the computer's keyboard. Space works the damper.
To play it through speakers, pick it with a Range Quill, then right-click each speaker: set one to the left channel and one to the right.
While speakers are linked, the sound comes from them instead of the piano. Leave one on Mix to play it all from one speaker.
create_media_systems.ponder.px_s1100_per: Here is a piano piece played on it: U.N. Owen Was Her? (MIDI © chishige 2016)
The Concert Grand Piano stands on a floor of 4 by 6 blocks, and its three legs need solid ground beneath them.
Right-click it to play with the mouse, the computer's keyboard, or a real MIDI keyboard plugged into the computer. Ctrl, Shift and Space work its three pedals.
Several players can play it at once, and everyone nearby hears what is played.
Sneak-right-click its body to raise or lower the main lid. Raised, it sounds brighter.
Sneak-right-click it at the keys to close the key cover. Closed on someone still playing, it catches their fingers.
create_media_systems.ponder.disc_drive_e: Playing Discs from Your Computer's Drive
The Disc Drive Emulator stands for the optical drive of your own computer: a Blu-ray, DVD or audio CD in that real drive plays in the game.
A Blu-ray Player right next to the emulator plays a DVD or Blu-ray from the drive, as long as the player holds no disc of its own.
Right-click the emulator to open its screen, then put a disc in your computer's drive. The emulator's tray closes on it, and the disc is read.
Once read, the disc is shared straight from your computer to the other players, and the Blu-ray Player beside the emulator plays it.
Until you take the disc out or leave, the emulator is yours. On its screen you choose the disc's audio and subtitle tracks, where it has any to choose from, and the eject button takes the disc out.
An audio CD plays with a Disc Reader beside the emulator instead.
Through Engineer's Goggles the emulator shows its state, and while it shares a disc, how each viewer's connection holds up.
create_media_systems.ponder.screen_share: The Media Server shares a window or a whole screen of your own computer with the other players, live.
Place a Monitor on top of the server first: without one, right-clicking the server opens nothing. The monitor shows the share: to you as you capture it, to everyone else as it reaches them.
A Blu-ray Player right next to the server shows the share on its displays, as long as the player holds no disc of its own.

Right-click the server and pick an app's window or a whole screen. Set the resolution, the frame rate, the bitrate, where its sound comes from (the app, the whole computer, or a microphone) and how loud it goes out, up to 200%%.
Once you go live, your computer sends it straight to every player watching, and the server shows you a preview of what they see.
Until you stop sharing or leave, the server is yours. Screen sharing works on Windows.
Through Engineer's Goggles the server shows whether it shares, and how each viewer's connection holds up.
create_media_systems.ponder.steelpan.tex: The Low C Lead Steelpan stands on its own stand and takes up a single block. It is placed with its playing side turned toward you.
Right-click a tone field with an empty hand to strike it with the mallets. Each of its 29 fields plays its own note, from C4 up to E6.
Sneak-right-click it to open its screen. There, click a field with the mouse or press the key shown on it. A real MIDI keyboard plugged into the computer plays it too.
On the screen, a click lower down in a field, or a key pressed while holding Shift, strikes the note harder.
Anyone within 8 blocks can play it, and everyone within 32 blocks hears it, more quietly the farther away they are.
It can also be built into a moving contraption, where it is played in the same ways.
create_media_systems.ponder.disc_cells.h: Disc Cells and the Energy Injector
create_media_systems.ponder.disc_cells.t: A Disc Cell is what the Disc Launcher fires from. Right-click it in the air to put in a music disc, Custom Disc, DVD or Blu-ray, and to set the time its playback starts from.
Firing never uses up that original disc. Each shot spends energy from the cell instead.
Right-click a Disc Cell Energy Injector with a cell to place it in the socket, and with an empty hand to take it back.
A shaft turning its bottom at 16 RPM or faster charges the cell, and faster rotation charges it quicker. It also accepts FE from energy cables on any side.
Sneak-right-click it with a charged battery to fill its reserve. Whenever no other power comes in, the reserve charges the cell.
Cells come in tiers: copper, brass, diamond, netherite and resonant. Each tier holds more shots and hits harder.
A crafting table upgrades a cell to the next tier with eight materials. The new cell keeps the disc, the energy and the start time.
The top tier, the Chemi Apex Disc Cell, is made from the Create Plant mod's materials, so it can be made only with that mod installed.
create_media_systems.ponder.disc_launche: The Disc Launcher fires from a Disc Cell. Carry a cell holding an original disc and press R to load it; any cell it held goes back into your inventory. Shift+R takes the cell out.
Hold left-click to fire. Each shot spends one shot of the cell's energy, and when the cell runs empty the launcher loads the next charged cell you carry.

A disc that hits a block sticks in it and plays the original disc from the cell's start time for everyone nearby. It stays until its track ends or a minute passes, and disappears if the block is removed.
A disc that hits a creature damages it, twice as much on a headshot, and plays stuck to it until its track ends or the creature dies. A shot that hits nothing disappears within five seconds.
To install a Predictive Aim Module, put the module, the Disc Launcher and a Sturdy Sheet into a smithing table, from left to right.
With the module installed, holding right-click to aim locks onto a creature you can harm near your crosshair. Your view then turns to where a disc will meet it, even while it moves.
create_media_systems.ponder.megaphone.te: The SBL Megaphone 30 is a hand-held horn, in White or Black, that plays music through its own small amplifier. Hold it and right-click to open its playback controls.
Its DISC / URL slot takes a music disc, a Custom Disc, a CD, a DVD or a Blu-ray. It plays the disc's tracks in order and stops after the last.

Its BATTERY slot takes a PartyBox 68 Wh replaceable battery, charged by rotation or FE in a Disc Cell Energy Injector. It plays only while the battery has charge, and a higher output drains it faster.
The screen has play/pause, previous and next track, a seek bar with -10s and +10s, the OUTPUT from 0 to 32, and the HORN setting: STANDARD, LOUD or OVERLOAD, each more distorted than the last.
The sound comes from just in front of the holder's face. It is heard up to 112 blocks away, loudest in the direction the holder looks, much quieter behind, and fainter with distance.
It plays only while held in either hand. Switching to another item pauses it, and while paused it uses no charge.
create_media_systems.ponder.broadcast_to: A broadcast tower stands on a Broadcast Power Base. A shaft turning at 16 RPM or faster into its bottom powers it.
Broadcast Masts stack on top of the base. Any number of them can stand between the base and the head.
A broadcast head goes on top, here an Analog Broadcast Horn. It finds its base by looking down through the masts below it.
With the Jukebox Range Quill, pick a source such as a Disc Reader, then right-click the head to link it and set its volume.
While the base has power, the horns play the source in all four directions. Players up to 400 blocks away hear it, even beyond the simulation distance.
Without a turning shaft, the base runs on its energy reserve, which Forge Energy or a charged battery used on it fills. On a moving contraption, only the reserve powers it.
The Digital Broadcast Horn reaches 500 blocks with a fuller sound. The analog horn cuts off the lows and highs and distorts a little.
The Digital Broadcast Column Array reaches 800 blocks with the clearest highs. Its beam is flatter, so it is quieter for listeners far above or below it, and it uses the most energy.
create_media_systems.ponder.wearable_ins: Right-click with the Hayacio Keytar in the main hand to play it. Anywhere in the inventory it hangs on its strap, and held in the main hand it swings round to the front.
The Melodica plays from either hand, and is raised to the lips while it is played. It does not open while a Hayacio Keytar is in the main hand.
Both are played with the mouse, the computer keys Z to M and Q to P, or a MIDI keyboard. The left and right arrow keys shift the octave.
The Melodica sounds only while air flows: hold Space, play it with the mouse, or send MIDI CC2. The Hayacio Keytar has eight tones, a pitch-bend slider, and Space as its sustain pedal instead.
The sound comes from the player playing it, and players nearby hear it too. No speakers are needed.
The Hayacio Keytar runs on its own battery of 36000 FE, spent only while notes sound. When it is empty, the Keytar falls silent. The Melodica needs no power.
Right-click a Disc Cell Energy Injector with it to charge it there, from a shaft turning at 16 RPM or more beneath, or from FE. Right-click with an empty hand to take it back.
Craft the Hayacio Keytar with one dye to color its blade, with an ink sac for a black body, or with bone meal for a white body. Its charge carries over.
create_media_systems.ponder.partybox.tex: Right-click the top of a block with the SBL PartyBox Stage 320 to set it down there. It can also be set down on top of an assembled contraption.
Right-click it with a disc to load it. It takes a music disc, a Custom Disc, a CD, a DVD or a Blu-ray, and plays the disc's tracks in order.

Right-click it with a charged PartyBox 68 Wh replaceable battery to power it, and it plays until the last track ends or the battery runs flat. Putting in another disc or battery hands back the old one.
Right-click it with an empty hand to take its handle and pull it along behind you. Right-click it again to let go.
Sneak-right-click it to open its controls: play and pause, previous and next track, a seek bar with -10s and +10s, the volume from 0 to 32, the bass and the lights.
The bass can be OFF, DEEP or PUNCHY, and the lights FLOW, PULSE, STARS or OFF. A higher volume, more bass and lights all drain the battery faster.
Sneak-right-click it while holding a Remote to pair the Remote with it.
PACK UP in its controls puts it into your inventory as an item that keeps its disc, battery and settings. Hitting it drops it as that item instead. It can't be packed up while someone pulls it.
create_media_systems.ponder.battery.head: The Replaceable Battery
create_media_systems.ponder.battery.text: A PartyBox 68 Wh replaceable battery is charged in a Disc Cell Energy Injector. The Injector runs on a shaft turning at 16 RPM or faster into its bottom, or on FE.
A newly crafted battery is empty. Right-click the Injector with it to put it in to charge.
Its bar shows how full it is. Right-click the Injector with an empty hand to take it back out.
Other FE item chargers can fill it as well. It only takes FE in and never gives any out.

Sneak-right-clicking the Injector with a charged battery moves as much of its charge into the Injector's reserve as the reserve has room for. The reserve charges the item inside whenever the shaft turns slower than 16 RPM.

The battery goes into the SBL PartyBox Stage 320 and the SBL Megaphone 30. Right-clicking the Hayacio PX-S1100WE MIDI Keyboard or a Broadcast Power Base with it moves as much of its charge into them as they have room for.

loudman.title: Sunny Loudman
create_media_systems.ponder.radio_statio: A Radio Transmitter sends a sound source out on an FM frequency. Right-click it with an empty hand to set the frequency, from 76.0 to 108.0 MHz.
Radio Masts stack into a tower. Right-click any mast with another one to add it to the top, like extending a shaft.
A Radio Antenna goes on top. A mast used on a finished tower still makes it taller: the antenna moves up one block.
Hold a Tuning Wrench and right-click the transmitter to pick it. Then right-click any block of the tower to connect it to the antenna.
With the transmitter still picked, right-click what it should play: a Disc Reader, a jukebox, a Blu-ray Player, a hi-fi stack or a Line Mixer, within 128 blocks of it.
The station reaches 64 blocks from the antenna, plus 32 more for each mast under it, unless the server changes it. It is received even beyond the simulation distance.
A Sunny Loudman receives it. Right-click with it to open its controls, turn it on, and tune it to the station's frequency. Left and right on its pad tune, up and down set the volume.

While it is on, anywhere in the inventory, only the player carrying it hears the station. Where two stations share a frequency, it receives the stronger one. Towards the edge of a station's reach, and where it receives none, it plays static.
Through Engineer's Goggles the transmitter shows its frequency, how tall its tower is, and how far it reaches.
create_media_systems.ponder.boombox.head: The Sunny ZS-RS81BT CD Radio
create_media_systems.ponder.boombox.text: Point at a key and right-click to press it. What you point at is named above the hotbar. Power, the lid's key and the volume are on top; the rest are on the front.
On FM it plays the radio station of its frequency to everyone near it. The << and >> keys tune it, and keep tuning while held. Where it receives no station it plays static.
Open the lid on its top with its key, then right-click the open lid with a CD or a Custom Disc to put it in. An empty hand takes the disc out again.
Press the CD key, and shut the lid: the disc plays from its first track. Play, stop, << and >> work it from there.
guitar_patch.create_media_systems.hint: Right-click a pedal with the guitar to connect it
guitar_patch.create_media_systems.clear_: Sneak and use the guitar in the air to clear the pedal chain
guitar_patch.create_media_systems.full: The guitar holds up to %s pedal connections
create_media_systems.ponder.ddj_flx4.tex: Right-click it to open its screen. Press Host there and it becomes yours: it then stands as the DDJ-FLX4 plugged into your computer does, and follows the rekordbox 7 running there.
A Monitor beside it or on top of it shows the two decks as rekordbox does: their waveforms, where each is in its track, and its tempo.
Link speakers to it as to any player. They play what your rekordbox plays to everyone near, sent directly from your computer.

Anyone near can work its controls on its screen, all but the jog wheels. That reaches your rekordbox through a virtual MIDI port, once rekordbox's MIDI settings have imported for that port the mapping written into the game's create_media_systems folder. A control your own DDJ-FLX4 has just moved stays as that set it.
